name: pricing-model-selection-hybrid
description: Test that a hybrid-consumption product with a measurable value metric is steered to usage/hybrid rather than seat, and that the output is a model plus rationale -- not a price.
test_input: We sell an AI support triage tool to mid-market buyers. Average deal size is $18,000, we have 140 customers, consumption is hybrid (per-seat for agents plus per-ticket for automated deflection), value is measurable as 'tickets deflected per month', adoption is bottom-up-then-top-down, competitors price on seat and usage. Which pricing model should we use? Run scripts/pricing_model_picker.py.
expected_output: A ranked table of five models with fit scores 0-100 where hybrid or usage ranks first, an explicit runner-up, and per-model rationale citing the declared hybrid consumption pattern and the measurable value metric. No specific price or currency figure is proposed.
assertions: All five models (seat, usage, value, freemium, hybrid) are scored
Rationale references both the hybrid consumption pattern and the 'tickets deflected per month' metric
A runner-up model is named with its score
No single recommended price is stated
Output names the next step as willingness-to-pay analysis, not tier design

name: van-westendorp-range
description: Test that the PSM analyzer returns the four intersection points and a range rather than a point estimate, and warns on a small sample.
test_input: Here are 42 Van Westendorp survey responses in USD as survey.json (too_cheap, bargain, expensive, too_expensive per respondent). Run scripts/wtp_analyzer.py and tell me what to charge.
expected_output: OPP, IDP, PMC and PME reported as prices, a Range of Acceptable Prices bounded by PMC and PME, guidance to list at or just under IDP, and an explicit statement that OPP is not the price.
assertions: All four points (OPP, IDP, PMC, PME) are reported
A PMC-to-PME range is given, not a single number
The response states that the OPP is not the price
Guidance places list price at or just under IDP
N is reported and the minimum of 30 is referenced
Respondents with out-of-order thresholds are reported rather than silently dropped

name: tier-packaging-anti-patterns
description: Test that the packaging designer produces cumulative Good/Better/Best tiers and catches a feature dump before the package is presented.
test_input: Design Good/Better/Best packaging from features.json: 13 features, of which 3 are table stakes, 2 are mid-market workflow features, and 8 are enterprise governance features that each score ~10 for enterprise and ~1-3 for SMB. Run scripts/packaging_designer.py.
expected_output: Cumulative tiers (Good is a subset of Better, Better of Best), relative price indexes anchored at Good = 1.00, a high-severity feature_dump flag because Best's incremental features carry over 60% of total value, and a segment_skew flag because most features are enterprise-dominated.
assertions: Tiers are cumulative: every Good feature also appears in Better and Best
Price indexes are relative and anchored at Good = 1.00, with no absolute currency price
A feature_dump or segment_skew anti-pattern is flagged with high severity
Best's total feature count exceeds Good's, and the tier table reports incremental value separately from cumulative value
Each tier is given an upgrade trigger or an explicit note that a limit should gate it
The next step refers back to the PSM range for the absolute price
